Emma — thanks for the clear ask. I’ve sketched an activation matrix and a minimal certification checklist (attached) to use with Procurement. High level plan below; attaching the matrix as activation_matrix_v1.xlsx.

High-level activation runway (target: 8-week window after PO clears):
1) Contract & capacity commitment (Week 0): PO signed, model(s) & peak QPS confirmed.
2) Fleet reservation & provisioning (Week 1–2): GPU pool reserved and nodes provisioned; basic smoke run.
3) Staging throughput validation (Week 3): 24–72 hour continuous throughput run with synthetic traffic matching sample profile.
4) Latency SLAs & KV warm cache validation (Week 4): p50/p95 under agreed thresholds with real prefix caching rehearsal.
5) Cost acceptance & fallback plan (Week 5): Validate per-token economics vs. hosted baseline and confirm fallback routing policies.
6) Cutover rehearsal & go/no-go (Week 6–7): Dress rehearsal during low-traffic window, rollback triggers exercised.
7) Go-live & monitoring guardrails (Week 8): Production switch, 72-hour elevated monitoring, and SLA attestation.

Acceptance gates (what we need from Minerva):
- Representative traffic sample (3 separate days of logs, masked PII)
- Target peak QPS and sustained QPS windows
- List of model versions and max sequence lengths to test
- Contact for procurement sign-off and SRE runbook owner

I’ve included a preliminary checklist in the attached PDF. Monica — please confirm staging cluster sizing assumptions for Minerva’s profile (I used 8x A100-80GB equiv for the initial run). Karthik — can you call out the quantization/throughput knobs we should test?

— Logan

Adding technical acceptance criteria and test vectors.

Suggested throughput validation matrix (staging):
- Baseline sustained run: 12 hours at 60% of projected sustained QPS (measure token throughput, GPU utilization, tail latency)
- Burst run: 15-minute ramp to 150% projected peak QPS (observe queuing/backpressure behavior)
- KV prefix warm: Repeated generation on 10k unique prefixes to evaluate cache hit ramp and latency delta
- Long-seq stress: 1-hour run on 4 longest sequence lengths to validate memory/kv stability

Quantization/instance permutations to test:
- FP16 default cluster vs 4-bit quantized variant (if Minerva opts for aggressive cost reduction)
- Batch size sweep: 1, 4, 8 — compare p95 and throughput for each profile

Pass/fail heuristics (examples):
- p95 latency increase <= 20% vs hosted baseline under equivalent QPS
- No OOMs or dropped requests during burst run
- Cost-per-token within +/- 10% of forecast (accounting for reserved discounts)

I’ll prep a short script to generate the synthetic traffic patterns if Minerva can confirm sequence length distributions.
